items.description: South Devon coast from Start Point to Dawlish Warren
items.eaAreaName: Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
items.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible 2 hours either side of high tide on Saturday morning. 
Areas particularly at risk include Torbay, Teignmouth, Beesands, Torcross, Slapton and Dawlish.

The high tide at Exmouth on Saturday is at 09:00, times of high water will vary along the coast.  Forecast total high tide level is 2.05mAOD, which is 0.27 metres above tide table level.  Force 6 southerly winds and offshore wave heights of over 1.7m are forecast over the high tide.

Coastal conditions should ease for Sunday morning high tide. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 3:00PM on Saturday 28 November or as the situation changes.

items.description: South Cornwall coast from Lizard Point to Gribbin Head excluding the Tidal Fal Estuary
items.eaAreaName: Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
items.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding.
Tidal conditions are expected to improve and no flooding is expected.  
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary. 
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

High tides over the next two days may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from this this morning from 05:30 to 11:00 and this evening from 18:00 - 22:45 (27/11/26). Locations most affected will be coastal roads and footpaths on the North Sea coast from Bridlington to Barmston. We are closely monitoring the situation. Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded. This message will be updated by 21:00 on Friday 27th November or as the situation changes.

floodArea.riverOrSea: South Cornwall Coast, Tidal Fal Estuary

items.message:
High tides and forecast weather conditions tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 

 

Flooding is possible up to 1 hour either side of high tide on Saturday morning. 

 

High water levels may cause flooding to quaysides, harbours, and low lying land, roads and car parks. 

   

High tide at Falmouth on Saturday is at 07:30AM, with a forecast tide level of 2.3mAOD, which is around 0.2m above tide table levels.  Times and heights of high tide will vary along the coast. Force 6 Southerly winds and offshore waves of around 1m are forecast over high tide. 

 

Coastal conditions should ease for Saturday evening's high tide.

floodArea.riverOrSea: River Hayle, Perrancoombe Stream, Bolingey Stream, Portreath Stream, Newlyn Coombe River

items.message:
High river levels over the next two days may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from the morning of Friday 27 November .
Catchments are saturated and river levels are rising in response to overnight rainfall.  The main areas of concern are low lying land and roads along the Hayle River. 
Further heavy rain is forecast over Friday night and Saturday morning causing rivers in the area to rise again.  The highest levels are forecast on Saturday afternoon, with flooding to riverside and low-lying land and roads expected. 
Rain is forecast to ease on Saturday afternoon, with river levels dropping by Sunday.
We are monitoring rainfall and river levels .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. Monitor local water levels and weather conditions.
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Saturday 28 November or as the situation changes.

Strong winds and large waves throughout the evening may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 19:15pm to 21:15pm on Friday 27th November and 08:00am and 10:00am on Saturday 28th November.
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers or on the coast, with spray being seen on the seafront paths. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. Please take notice of the Flood Sign at the top of South Beach Road. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Kings Lynn of 3.36mAODN at 20:15pm, on Friday 27th November, Wind Force 6, Southerly, and 3.17mAOD at 09:00am, on Saturday 28th November, Wind Force 7, South-easterly.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  
This message will be updated by 4:44PM on Friday 27 November or as the situation changes.
